proposals.title: Robust Spatial Trajectory and Domain Integration with Expression Pattern Discovery
proposals.summary: This proposal presents a comprehensive framework that emphasizes learning spatially coherent trajectories and delineating spatial domains while simultaneously uncovering spatial expression patterns. The analysis will begin with rigorous quality control and normalization to address sparsity and uneven sampling, followed by spatially aware dimensionality reduction and graph construction. Special emphasis is placed on sensitivity analyses to ensure robust neighborhood definitions. The method further integrates pseudotime inference to capture continuous biological transitions and leverages differential expression and gene signature scoring to highlight spatial expression patterns. Additionally, exploratory measures for cell–cell communication are incorporated by correlating spatially proximal gene expression signatures. This integrated approach primarily targets spatial trajectory inference and domain delineation, while also providing key insights into expression pattern discovery and potential intercellular interactions.

proposals.title: Sensitivity-Optimized Spatial Trajectory Inference with Parameter Tuning
proposals.summary: Focusing primarily on the extraction of spatially coherent trajectories, this analysis emphasizes sensitivity optimization through cross-validation for neighborhood parameter tuning. The workflow begins with robust preprocessing and spatial smoothing tailored for high-dimensional spatial transcriptomics data. It then applies spatially informed dimensionality reduction and graph-based methods to delineate trajectories that respect the physical organization of tissues. While the main goal is to capture continuous state transitions, the proposal also includes secondary objectives such as delineating spatial domains and identifying spatial expression gradients. Preliminary analyses of cell–cell communication signals through marker gene co-expression in adjacent spots will further validate the trajectory models, ensuring that the inferred paths are both biologically and statistically robust.

proposals.title: Anatomically Validated Domain Delineation and Pseudotemporal Mapping
proposals.summary: This proposal integrates spatial domain delineation with pseudotemporal trajectory mapping, taking advantage of anatomical validation to ground computational findings in tissue architecture. After rigorous preprocessing and spatial smoothing to mitigate data irregularities, the method employs spatially aware clustering algorithms to segment the tissue into discrete domains. Pseudotime inference is then applied within and between these domains to capture continuous state transitions and developmental progressions. The approach explicitly targets the goals of learning spatial trajectories and delineating precise tissue compartments, while also assessing spatial expression patterns using differential expression analyses. Furthermore, the strategy incorporates preliminary cell–cell communication analyses by evaluating co-localization of ligand-receptor pairs, ensuring that the inferred trajectories align with known anatomical and signaling structures.

proposals.title: Multi-Resolution Integration for Domain Delineation and Transition Mapping
proposals.summary: This analysis employs a multi-resolution strategy to capture both discrete tissue compartments and subtle continuous transitions across spatial transcriptomics datasets. Starting with robust quality control and spatial smoothing, the pipeline uses spatially aware, multi-resolution clustering to dissect domain boundaries and reveal underlying gradients of gene expression. The integrated approach explicitly targets spatial domain delineation and the identification of spatially coherent trajectories by leveraging pseudotime inference at various resolutions. Additionally, differential expression analysis aids in discovering spatial expression patterns, and exploratory network inference techniques are applied to uncover potential cell–cell communication signals between identified clusters. This proposal provides a scalable and validated framework for dissecting the layered complexity of tissue organization.

proposals.title: Integrated Spatial Dynamics: Domain Segmentation and State Transition Analysis
proposals.summary: Aiming at a balanced exploration of tissue dynamics, this proposal integrates domain segmentation with state transition analysis. The methodology initiates with stringent preprocessing and spatial smoothing to overcome inherent data challenges, followed by spatially informed dimensionality reduction. Clustering techniques are used to delineate sharp tissue boundaries, while pseudotime inference captures gradual biological transitions across adjacent domains. This dual focus ensures that both discrete and continuous aspects of tissue organization are explicitly addressed. The proposal also includes targeted differential expression analyses for spatial expression pattern discovery and a preliminary evaluation of cell–cell communication by assessing spatial correlations in signaling molecule genes, thereby encapsulating the four core aims of spatial omics analysis.

proposals.title: Robust Preprocessing and Continuum Inference for Spatial Expression and Communication
proposals.summary: This proposal is centered on leveraging robust preprocessing techniques and continuum inference methods to explore spatial expression patterns and potential cell–cell communication networks. The analysis begins with rigorous normalization and spatial smoothing to handle data sparsity and variability, followed by spatially aware dimensionality reduction that respects local neighborhoods. The primary focus is on uncovering continuous gradients in gene expression—indicative of spatially coherent biological transitions—and delineating subtle spatial domains from these gradients. Importantly, the approach integrates network analysis to infer cell–cell communication by detecting co-varying gene modules in neighboring tissue regions. In this way, the work directly addresses the discovery of spatial expression patterns and the analysis of cell–cell interactions, while also supporting supplementary trajectory and domain analysis.

proposals.title: Statistically Rigorous Pseudotemporal and Domain Analysis with Communication Insights
proposals.summary: This project proposes a statistically rigorous framework that combines pseudotime trajectory inference with refined domain segmentation, supplemented by an exploration of cell–cell communication. The analysis pipeline applies enhanced quality control, spatially aware dimensionality reduction, and optimized neighborhood graph construction to capture both continuous and discrete changes in tissue organization. Primary goals include learning spatial trajectories through pseudotime estimation and delineating clear tissue domains using clustering techniques. Simultaneously, differential expression and marker gene analyses are employed to detect spatial expression patterns. The innovative component of this proposal lies in the integration of communication analysis, where spatial co-expression of known ligand-receptor pairs is examined to reveal interaction networks, thereby strengthening the biological interpretation of the results.

proposals.title: Cross-Validated Multi-Resolution Analysis for Gene Expression Landscapes and State Transitions
proposals.summary: Designed to robustly address the inherent complexity of spatial transcriptomics data, this proposal employs cross-validation and multi-resolution clustering to build a comprehensive picture of gene expression landscapes. The approach emphasizes the extraction of spatially coherent trajectories through pseudotime analysis, alongside the delineation of distinct tissue domains. Rigorous cross-validation techniques ensure that the neighborhood graph construction and parameter tuning are optimized for reliable spatial inference. Differential expression analysis is then used to uncover spatial expression patterns that correlate with both domain boundaries and continuous transitions. Additionally, initial network analyses are integrated to assess potential cell–cell communication by examining spatially proximal interactions, ensuring a holistic interpretation of tissue state transitions.

proposals.title: Dynamic Tissue Domain Analysis Anchored in Spatial Robustness and Communication Networks
proposals.summary: This proposal focuses on dynamically mapping tissue organization by robustly delineating spatial domains and linking them to continuous state transitions and communication networks. It starts with a thorough preprocessing routine that includes normalization and spatial smoothing, followed by sensitivity-optimized, spatially informed clustering to segment tissue regions. Pseudotime techniques are subsequently applied to map dynamic trajectories within and between these domains, capturing gradual biological changes. The analysis also emphasizes the discovery of spatial expression patterns through targeted differential analyses, and uniquely integrates the evaluation of cell–cell communication by analyzing co-expression of ligand-receptor modules across domain boundaries. By explicitly addressing all four key aims—trajectory inference, domain delineation, pattern discovery, and communication analysis—this proposal offers a complete strategy for dissecting complex tissue architectures.

plan.user_request: Coordinate domain agents to propose exactly nine computational spatial-omics analyses, via draft, critique, and final synthesis steps, producing final_proposals.json without executing the analyses.

steps.title: Draft nine spatial analysis proposals
steps.description: Use the Spatial-CV Planning Agent (spatial_cv_agent) to generate an initial set of exactly nine computational spatial-omics analysis proposals grounded solely in the provided background (spatially aware trajectories, domain delineation, expression-pattern discovery, and communication analysis). Save these as a JSON object at project/outputs/hypotheses/draft_proposals.json, with whatever internal structure is most convenient for later critique and synthesis.
steps.reasoning: This step creates concrete candidate analyses, tailored to spatial transcriptomics and the described goals of spatially aware trajectories and communication analysis, that downstream agents can systematically critique and refine; spatial_cv_agent is explicitly required to own this drafting stage.
steps.assignment_rationale: spatial_cv_agent is explicitly required for this TA+CV treatment and is specialized for drafting exactly nine spatial-analysis proposals, writing draft_proposals.json as specified.

steps.title: Critique draft proposals
steps.description: Have the Critic agent read project/outputs/hypotheses/draft_proposals.json and evaluate all nine proposals for clarity, feasibility on spatial transcriptomics data, distinctness from each other, and alignment with the background aims (learning spatially coherent trajectories, delineating domains, supporting pattern discovery and cell–cell communication analysis). Record structured feedback, including per-proposal strengths, weaknesses, and revision instructions, in project/outputs/hypotheses/critique.json.
steps.reasoning: A dedicated critique phase ensures that the drafted analyses are internally consistent, biologically and computationally plausible, and well matched to the spatial-trajectory focus before finalization; the Critic agent is the appropriate specialist to produce the requested critique.json once the draft artifact exists.
steps.assignment_rationale: critic_agent is the dedicated review-only critic that produces hypotheses/critique.json, matching the step’s need to evaluate the nine drafts and write structured feedback to critique.json.

steps.title: Synthesize final proposal set
steps.description: Use the Hypothesis/Proposal-Synthesis agent to combine project/outputs/hypotheses/draft_proposals.json and project/outputs/hypotheses/critique.json into a finalized set of exactly nine spatial-omics analysis proposals. Revise titles and expand summaries following the critique while maintaining close coherence with the spatially aware analysis description, and write project/outputs/hypotheses/final_proposals.json as a JSON object whose only top-level key is "proposals", containing an array of nine items where each item has only "title" and a detailed "summary"; do not execute any of the proposed analyses.
steps.reasoning: This final synthesis step transforms the critiqued drafts into a clean, paper-style proposal set with the exact required structure and cardinality, ensuring that the single deliverable final_proposals.json is ready for downstream use while respecting the constraint that no actual analyses are run.
steps.assignment_rationale: hypothesis_agent is designed for proposal drafting and final synthesis, and it is the appropriate specialist to read the draft and critique and write the finalized nine-item hypotheses/final_proposals.json.
